title: Rama's servant
hookLine: a monkey tears up Ravana's favorite garden, leaving one tree standing, and then announces exactly whose servant he is
carry: dasya bhakti: i am rama's servant

lines: DAWN, AND THE GROVE COMES DOWN.
cards: At dawn, the birds of the ashoka grove start up in alarm. Trees crash down. Pools are churned to mud.
Pavilions come apart. Ravana's most beautiful garden is being taken apart by something huge. The guards wake, and they notice something odd.
In the middle of the wreckage, one tree is left untouched: the one Sita sits beneath.

teach.b: The rakshasi guards turn to Sita. Who is that? What did he say to you?
How would I know? Rakshasas are the ones who change shape at will. You'd know better than I would.
She protects Hanuman and gives them nothing. The guards run to Ravana, who sends a great company of armed servants to capture the monkey. Hanuman is waiting for them on the gateway arch.
He grows huge, slaps his arms, and roars a declaration, which Valmiki gives in full. Victory to Rama, mighty in strength, and to Lakshmana. Victory to King Sugriva.

teach.h: I AM THE SERVANT OF RAMA.
teach.b: I am the servant of the lord of Kosala, Rama. I am Hanuman, son of the wind. Notice the order.
In the enemy's capital, at the start of a fight, he says whose servant he is before he says who he is.

teach.h: DASYA BHAKTI: THE LOVE OF A SERVANT.
teach.b: Hindus have a name for this love: dasya bhakti, loving God as a servant loves a master he adores.
It's why, in so many Hindu homes and temples, the picture of Rama's court shows Hanuman kneeling at Rama's feet, hands folded.

The strongest one in the room chooses the lowest place, and devotees see that as his greatness, not his weakness. Then the servants rush him. Hanuman snatches up an iron bar from the gateway and drives them back.
It's only the first wave. Lanka is about to show him its strength.

how: Hanuman's declaration of victory to Rama and of himself as Rama's servant is recited by devotees, and some see in it the heart of Hanuman's devotion, dāsya, the love of a servant.

o: Hanuman's stand at the gate as Rama's servant
a duel between Rama and Ravana on the beach
the monkeys' war on Lanka's walls after the bridge

games.q: the first wave — tap the pairs.
p: his weapon against the first wave

s: Hanuman destroys the whole grove, Sita's tree included
he leaves the tree where Sita sits untouched.
Hanuman fights the first wave with a sword
he snatches up an iron bar from the gateway.
Hanuman declares himself the servant of Rama
dāso 'haṃ kosalendrasya: I am the servant of the lord of Kosala.

games.q: you're Hanuman, standing on the gateway of the enemy's city, facing an army. what do you announce first?
o: victory to Rama, and that you are his servant.
games.why: Hanuman proclaims victory to Rama, Lakshmana and Sugriva, and calls himself the servant of the lord of Kosala, before naming himself.

practice: If you have a family shrine or a picture of Hanuman, fold your hands and say softly, Jai Shri Ram, or simply Rama's name, putting him first the way Hanuman did.
If you don't pray, ask yourself gently: what do I serve and love, a family, a craft, a friend, a good? Name it before you name anything about yourself, and breathe with it.

wordCard.voice: The fight. Hanuman wrecks Ravana's grove but spares Sita's tree, declares himself Rama's servant from the gateway, and drives back the first wave of guards.

orig.note: Sanskrit dāsa, servant: dāso 'haṃ, 'I am the servant'.

carryVoice: Your line: dasya bhakti: i am rama's servant. Tomorrow, Lanka sends its best. See you then.

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Sundara Kanda 41–42 (the grove destroyed; Sita's answer to the guards; the first wave)
